nobox.final_span:
the company managed only one successful orbital rocket booster reflight. It tried to achieve this twice previously, however, CG tests indicated cracks in the first stage of the rocket, resulting in failures that halted the company's ambitious goals to retrieve and reuse rocket boosters.
After the SES-10 mission, SpaceX is once again showing the possibility of perfect reusability. The company constructed its next Falcon 9 booster using a rocket segment that had flown previously twice, and maintained a schedule for a potential launch in the upcoming month.
The full-up Falcon 9 booster that launched SES-10 is seen after landing on the drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You" in the Atlantic Ocean. The booster will be reflown in late May, SpaceX announced on April 8, 2017
